prior_year_events.impact_description: We also saw deterioration in attritional and large losses in a number of short tail lines. In Marine we saw large losses in Onshore Energy, Hull and Asia and attritional development on one large coverholder in Marine Liability (all of which led to us either exiting the business or in the case of Marine liability not renewing the relationship during 2019). In Property we saw attritional development in both our direct and binder books which led to further remediation activities.

named_events.loss_description: Our total losses from Covid-19 amount to GBP 66.5m. They are largely contained within our Contingency account and mainly relate to event cancellation cover.
Losses from Natural Catastrophes had a material impact on our result, worsening the Combined Ratio by 11.2 percentage points.

data.standardized_narrative: In 2020, Syndicate 1200 reported an overall deterioration of GBP 6.8 million in its prior year claims provisions. This strengthening is attributed to the inherent uncertainty in claims estimation. The 2018 year of account, now a prior year, experienced deterioration in attritional and large losses across short tail lines, Marine, Onshore Energy, Hull, Asia, Marine Liability, and Property. Catastrophe events like Hurricanes Florence and Michael and California wildfires also impacted the 2018 year. The current year (2020) was significantly impacted by GBP 66.5 million in Covid-19 related losses, primarily in the Contingency book, and material losses from Natural Catastrophes.

data.data_quality_notes: The claims development triangle is distorted by the Reinsurance To Close (RITC) of the 2017 and prior years of account into Syndicate 3500, making it unreliable for calculating prior year development. The stated overall deterioration figure of GBP 6.8m is used instead. The gross premium mix includes a negative value for Aviation, as presented in the source table.
